                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The S-polynomial.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.BokutShiaoCornerUneq.resolves {n : ℕ} (hp : HeckeParams) {i''' i'' i' i : Fin n} (hn : 0 < n) (hi' : ↑i' + 1 = ↑i) (hi'' : ↑i'' + 1 = ↑i') (hi''' : ↑i''' + 1 = ↑i'') :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      ∃ (nf : AlgElement (HeckeGen n) ℝ), ReducesToNF (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (oc i''' i'' i' i hi' hi'' hi''').spoly nf ∧ nf.isZero

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Fifteen steps, to zero, with no quadratic rule anywhere.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      §4ab Depths i−2 and i−3 — the mirror of §4aa, and not its mirror image #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      (a, b) = (2, 3): the depths of §4aa the other way round. That does not transpose the chain — §4aa needs no quadratic rule at all and runs in fifteen steps, this one needs two and runs in nineteen. The asymmetry is real: the two depths enter the S-polynomial in different positions,

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      spoly = D₁ σᵢ₋₁ σᵢ E₂  −  σᵢ₋₁ D₁ E₂ σᵢ

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      so swapping them is not a symmetry of the problem.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      With x = σᵢ, y = σᵢ₋₁, z = σᵢ₋₂, w = σᵢ₋₃, here D₁ = xyz and E₂ = yzw:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      spoly = x y z y x y z w  −  y x y z y z w x

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Seventeen of the nineteen steps apply a two-word monic rule and go through monicStep; the two quadratic ones, at steps 4 and 7, are written out and are where h enters. It leaves at step 11, where z y x z y z w and z y z x y z w carry h with opposite signs — the same cancellation shape as §4z, and again the pair is carried unmerged rather than costing a step.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Nine rules occur: the braid rule at each of the three adjacent pairs, all three far-commutations, the Bokut–Shiao rule at (i−2,i−1,i−3), and the composition's own two rules. Every helper they need was already proved in §4aa.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.BokutShiaoCornerLow.oc_spoly_coeff {n : ℕ} (hp : HeckeParams) {i''' i'' i' i : Fin n} (hi' : ↑i' + 1 = ↑i) (hi'' : ↑i'' + 1 = ↑i') (hi''' : ↑i''' + 1 = ↑i'') (m : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          (oc i''' i'' i' i hi' hi'' hi''').spoly.coeff m = (S0 hp i''' i'' i' i).coeff m

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The S-polynomial.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.BokutShiaoCornerLow.resolves {n : ℕ} (hp : HeckeParams) {i''' i'' i' i : Fin n} (hn : 0 < n) (hi' : ↑i' + 1 = ↑i) (hi'' : ↑i'' + 1 = ↑i') (hi''' : ↑i''' + 1 = ↑i'') :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          ∃ (nf : AlgElement (HeckeGen n) ℝ), ReducesToNF (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (oc i''' i'' i' i hi' hi'' hi''').spoly nf ∧ nf.isZero

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Nineteen steps, to zero.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          §4ac Both depths at i−3 — the last composition, and the longest #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          (a, b) = (3, 3), twenty-five steps: the largest single obligation in the arc, and the one that closes the n = 4 enumeration. Structurally it is §4z at one more level of depth — the Bokut–Shiao rule against itself, both depths pinned at i − 3 — and it inherits §4z's shape exactly: two quadratic steps, an h that enters there and cancels in the middle, and everything else a two-word monic rule.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          With x = σᵢ, y = σᵢ₋₁, z = σᵢ₋₂, w = σᵢ₋₃, descWord i j₁ = xyzw and descWord i−1 j₂ = yzw:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          spoly = x y z w y x y z w  −  y x y z w y z w x

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Twenty-three of the twenty-five steps go through monicStep; the two quadratic ones are at steps 5 and 9, both at σᵢ₋₃, and h cancels at step 17 where z y z x w y z w and z y z w x y z w meet with opposite signs.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Its length is not a sign of extra difficulty — reducing the two terms separately takes 12 and 13 steps, and 12 + 13 = 25. Every corner case is exactly the sum of its two reductions; this one just has the longest pair.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Twenty-five steps, to zero — the last composition of the n = 4 enumeration.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      §4ad B × B at general depth: the whole b = 2 column #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      §4z–§4ac closed the Bokut–Shiao-against-Bokut–Shiao corner at four fixed depths, (a, b) ∈ {(2,2), (3,2), (2,3), (3,3)}, writing a = i − j₁ and b = i − j₂. Those are cases, not a family. The chain length is quadratic in the depths — 2ab − a² + 5a + 1 steps when a ≤ b, b² + 3b + 5 when a > b — so no fixed script covers the corner, and the general statement needs an induction on both.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      This section takes the first genuinely general slice: b = 2, and a arbitrary. It is the tractable half, because in the a > b regime the length does not depend on a at all — the extra depth rides along inertly rather than contributing work. That is precisely what the proof exhibits. Writing

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      x = σᵢ,   y = σᵢ₋₁,   z = σᵢ₋₂,   u = σᵢ₋₃,   E = descWord (i−3) j

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      so that descWord i j = x y z E, every one of the seventeen words in the chain has the shape

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      (explicit prefix) ++ E ++ (explicit suffix)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      and E is never inspected — not by a rule, not by a distinctness obligation. The chain is fifteen steps at every depth, all of them monic, so monicStep (§4x) discharges the lot and the deformation parameter h never appears.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The only hypothesis on the depth is j ≤ i − 3, so this subsumes §4aa, which is the case j = i − 3 (there E = [σᵢ₋₃]). §4aa is kept rather than replaced because its chain is the one the confluence engine produces at that depth: when j = i − 3 the rule used at steps 5 and 13 degenerates to the braid word, and the engine picks the Yang–Baxter rule sharing that leading monomial — a rule of leading coefficient −1, which is why §4aa reads differently step for step. Both rules are in the completed system and both chains are valid.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Six rules occur. Three are Bokut–Shiao at the general bottom j, with tops i, i−1 and i−2; one is the fixed-depth Bokut–Shiao at (i−2, i−1, i−3) (§4aa's, reused); and three are far-commutations, σᵢσᵢ₋₂, σᵢσᵢ₋₃ and σᵢ₋₁σᵢ₋₃. Every distinctness obligation is settled by a first, second, third or fourth letter among the four generators, which is what leaves the depth free.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Why fifteen. Reducing the two terms of the S-polynomial separately takes 8 and 7 steps, and 8 + 7 = 15: as in every other corner case, the chain is exactly the two independent reductions with no shared intermediate to cut. Here that split is visible in the stage list — V0 ⋯ V8 is the first term's reduction, U0 ⋯ U7 the second's, and they meet at V8 = U7.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Fifteen steps, to zero, at every depth j ≤ i − 3.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          §4ae The corner's b = 3 column #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          §4ad closed the corner's b = 2 column for every depth a. This is the same statement one level down: b = 3, and a arbitrary. Naming the generators by distance below the top index — i₀ = σᵢ, i₁ = σᵢ₋₁, … — and writing E = descWord i₄ j for the part of the descending run that grows with a, every word is again (explicit prefix) ++ E ++ (explicit suffix) with E never inspected. Twenty-three steps, all monic, h never appears, and the only hypothesis on the depth is j ≤ i − 4.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          What the extra level costs, exactly. Setting the two columns side by side with rules named relatively, the b = 3 chain is the b = 2 chain with one block inserted twice — once into each term's reduction:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          b = 2:  B₂₁ F₀₂ │ B₂₁ F₀₂ B₃₂ F₁₃ F₀₃                    │ B₁₀ B₂₁⁽ᵛ⁾ │ B₁₀ B₂₁ F₀₂ B₃₂ F₁₃ F₀₃
b = 3:  B₂₁ F₀₂ │ B₂₁ F₀₂ B₃₂ F₁₃ F₀₃ ⟨B₄₃ F₂₄ F₁₄ F₀₄⟩  │ B₁₀ B₂₁⁽ᵛ⁾ │ B₁₀ B₂₁ F₀₂ B₃₂ F₁₃ F₀₃ ⟨B₄₃ F₂₄ F₁₄ F₀₄⟩

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The inserted block is one Bokut–Shiao step at the next generator down, then a run of far-commutations carrying the newly exposed letter leftwards past the prefix. Its length is b + 1, so steps(b) = steps(b−1) + 2(b + 1) from steps(2) = 15, which is the b² + 3b + 5 the rank sweep fitted: 15, 23, 33, …

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          That far-commutation run is not new work in disguise — it is exactly farComm_transport_left (§4v), a low generator moving left past a run of generators that all far-commute with it, whose side condition descWord_index_ge already supplies. Writing the column out step by step, as here, is the honest thing to do while b is fixed; the transport lemma is what an induction on b would have to use instead, because there the block's length is not a constant.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Both this section and §4ad are emitted from the confluence engine's own trace rather than transcribed: the generator was checked by re-deriving §4ad's seventeen words and fifteen rules and finding them identical.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Why twenty-three. Reducing the two terms of the S-polynomial separately takes 12 and 11 steps, and 12 + 11 = 23. The first term runs V0 ⋯ V11 and then one further step onto the second term's endpoint, which is why the section has no V12: that word is U11, reached from the other side. As in every corner case the chain is exactly the two independent reductions, with no shared intermediate to cut.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.BokutShiaoCornerDepth3.oc_spoly_coeff {n : ℕ} {i₀ i₁ i₂ i₃ i₄ j : Fin n} (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i₀) (h₂ : ↑i₂ + 1 = ↑i₁) (h₃ : ↑i₃ + 1 = ↑i₂) (h₄ : ↑i₄ + 1 = ↑i₃) (hj : ↑j ≤ ↑i₄) (m : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            (oc i₀ i₁ i₂ i₃ i₄ j h₁ h₂ h₃ h₄ hj).spoly.coeff m = (T0 i₀ i₁ i₂ i₃ i₄ j).coeff m

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The S-polynomial.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.BokutShiaoCornerDepth3.resolves {n : ℕ} (hp : HeckeParams) {i₀ i₁ i₂ i₃ i₄ j : Fin n} (hn : 0 < n) (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i₀) (h₂ : ↑i₂ + 1 = ↑i₁) (h₃ : ↑i₃ + 1 = ↑i₂) (h₄ : ↑i₄ + 1 = ↑i₃) (hj : ↑j ≤ ↑i₄) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ∃ (nf : AlgElement (HeckeGen n) ℝ), ReducesToNF (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (oc i₀ i₁ i₂ i₃ i₄ j h₁ h₂ h₃ h₄ hj).spoly nf ∧ nf.isZero

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            23 steps, to zero, at every depth j ≤ i − 4.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            §4af The block that drives the whole a > b corner #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            §4ad and §4ae close the corner's b = 2 and b = 3 columns by writing their fifteen and twenty-three steps out one at a time. That does not scale: the chain is b² + 3b + 5 steps long, so column b needs a longer script than column b − 1 and no fixed script covers them all.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            It does not have to. Setting the two columns side by side shows the chain is not a flat list of steps but a loop over a single index, and this section proves the body of that loop once and for all.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Write D = descWord i j₁ for the long run and j₂ for the short one. The claim is that both terms of the S-polynomial march down through the invariants

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            V side:   R ++ D ++ descWord k j₂                →  (R ++ [σ_{k−1}]) ++ D ++ descWord (k−1) j₂
U side:   Q ++ D ++ descWord k j₂ ++ [σᵢ]        →  (Q ++ [σ_{k−1}]) ++ D ++ descWord (k−1) j₂ ++ [σᵢ]

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            as k runs from i down past j₂, and that each pass is the same two moves:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • one Bokut–Shiao step at top k, which is available because the letter σ_k ending descWord k j₁ inside D is immediately followed by the σ_k that heads descWord k j₂ — the two runs meet exactly there, which is what makes the redex bsWord₁ k j₁; and
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • one leftward transport of the newly exposed σ_{k−1} across the letters of D lying above k, which is farComm_transport_left (§4v), its side condition supplied by descWord_index_ge (every letter of a descending run from i down to k+1 has index > (k−1) + 1).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            blockStep below is that pass. The part of D above k enters as an abstract Y rather than as descWord i (k+1), which costs nothing and avoids naming k + 1 — needed, since the first pass has k = i and no such index exists.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The counts this predicts are exactly the measured ones. The V side runs the loop for k = i down to j₂, preceded by two setup steps; the U side runs it for k = i−1 down to j₂ and is followed by two closing steps. Each pass at depth d = i − k costs 1 + d, so

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            V = 2 + (b+1) + b(b+1)/2,   U = b + b(b+1)/2 + 2,   V + U = b² + 3b + 5

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            matching the confluence engine at every b from 2 to 7 and every a > b, including a = b + 1, where the engine's own deg-lex strategy interleaves the passes differently but the chain built from these blocks is still a legal reduction — a SingleStepReduction may rewrite any redex, not only the largest.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.descWord_of_lt {n : ℕ} {i j : Fin n} (hij : ↑i < ↑j) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            descWord i j = []

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            A descending run from below its own floor is empty.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.descWord_cons_le {n : ℕ} {i' i j : Fin n} (hi : ↑i' + 1 = ↑i) (hj : ↑j ≤ ↑i) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            descWord i j = { index := i } :: descWord i' j

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            descWord_cons at the boundary. The original needs the floor to lie at or below i − 1; this needs it only at or below i, the extra case being j = i, where the tail is empty rather than a shorter run. The corner loop's last pass is exactly that case, so it cannot use the original.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.blockStep {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ j₂ k kd : Fin n} (hk : ↑kd + 1 = ↑k) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑kd) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑k) (Y R S : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (hY : ∀ y ∈ Y, ↑kd + 1 < ↑y.index) (hD : descWord i j₁ = Y ++ { index := k } :: descWord kd j₁) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (hne : ∀ q ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), q ≠ R ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k j₂ ++ S))) (hcol : ∀ (u v : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), u ++ v = Y → u ≠ [] → ∀ q ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), q ≠ R ++ (u ++ { index := kd } :: (v ++ ({ index := k } :: descWord kd j₁ ++ (descWord kd j₂ ++ S))))) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (R ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k j₂ ++ S)), c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (R ++ { index := kd } :: (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord kd j₂ ++ S)), c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            One pass of the corner loop: a Bokut–Shiao step at top k, then the newly exposed σ_{k−1} carried left across Y.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Y is the part of the long run descWord i j₁ lying above k; R is whatever has already accumulated to the left, S whatever trails on the right (empty on the V side, [σᵢ] on the U side). The two collision hypotheses are the ones monicStep and farComm_transport_left ask for: the other terms of the element must miss the word being rewritten, and must miss every word the transport passes through.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.blockStep_top {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ j₂ kd : Fin n} (hk : ↑kd + 1 = ↑i) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑kd) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑kd) (R S : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (hne : ∀ q ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), q ≠ R ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord i j₂ ++ S))) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (R ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord i j₂ ++ S)), c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (R ++ { index := kd } :: (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord kd j₂ ++ S)), c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The loop's first pass, where k = i and nothing lies above it: Y is empty and the transport is the identity, so the pass is the Bokut–Shiao step alone. Only two non-collision facts are needed, one per endpoint — with Y empty the transport passes through no intermediate word.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.loop {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ j₂ e ed : Fin n} (hed : ↑ed + 1 = ↑e) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑ed) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑e) (S : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (m : ℕ) (k kd : Fin n) (A Y : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ↑kd + 1 = ↑k → ↑k = ↑e + m → (∀ y ∈ Y, ↑kd + 1 < ↑y.index) → descWord i j₁ = Y ++ { index := k } :: descWord kd j₁ → MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(A ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k j₂ ++ S)), c)]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(A ++ (descWord kd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c)])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The loop. blockStep iterated: k walks down from its starting value to e, one pass per index, and what those passes leave behind is the descending run descWord kd ed accumulated in front.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The induction is on the number of passes still to come. It carries Y — the part of the long run lying above k — as a parameter rather than as descWord i (k+1), so each pass hands the next one Y ++ [σ_k] and no index above k is ever named.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Stated for a single term, where the collision hypotheses of blockStep are vacuous. That is the whole combinatorial content of the a > b corner: what remains for the two-term S-polynomial is bookkeeping about which words the bystanding term must avoid, not further rewriting.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.loopFromTop {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ j₂ e ed idd : Fin n} (m : ℕ) (hed : ↑ed + 1 = ↑e) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑ed) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑e) (hid : ↑idd + 1 = ↑i) (hm : ↑i = ↑e + m) (A S : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(A ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord i j₂ ++ S)), c)]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(A ++ (descWord idd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c)])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The loop, entered at the top. The first pass has k = i, so nothing of the long run lies above it and Y is empty; m is the number of passes less one. This is the form the corner's two terms are actually reduced by, and it witnesses that loop's hypotheses are satisfiable.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Carrying a bystanding term through the loop #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The corner's S-polynomial has two terms, so each pass of the loop rewrites one while the other sits by, and blockStep must be told the bystander is not the word being rewritten. Two facts make that uniform.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            First, the bystander does not move. At pass k it is A ++ descWord kd ed ++ ⋯, and after the pass A has grown by σ_kd while the run has shortened to descWord kdd ed — so A ++ [σ_kd] ++ descWord kdd ed is again A ++ descWord kd ed. It is literally the same word at every pass.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Second, every word a pass rewrites begins, after A, with σ_i, the head of the long run: the pass's own source is A ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ ⋯), and each word the transport visits is A ++ (u ++ ⋯) with u a non-empty prefix of the part of the long run above k. The bystander instead begins with σ_kd, and kd < i. So one letter separates the bystander from everything in sight.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.append_cons_ne {n : ℕ} {A B C : Monomial (HeckeGen n)} {x y : HeckeGen n} (hxy : x ≠ y) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            A ++ x :: B ≠ A ++ y :: C

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Two words with a common prefix differ as soon as the next letter does.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.pass_hne {n : ℕ} {i j₁ j₂ k kd ed : Fin n} (hji : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑i) (hedkd : ↑ed ≤ ↑kd) (hkdi : ↑kd < ↑i) (A S : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c' : ℝ) (q : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            q ∈ List.map Prod.fst ([] ++ [(A ++ (descWord kd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c')]) → q ≠ A ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k j₂ ++ S))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The bystander is not the word the pass rewrites.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
