                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.pass_hcol {n : ℕ} {i j₁ j₂ k kd ed : Fin n} (hedkd : ↑ed ≤ ↑kd) (A S Y : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c' : ℝ) (hY : ∀ y ∈ Y, ↑kd + 1 < ↑y.index) (u v : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            u ++ v = Y → u ≠ [] → ∀ q ∈ List.map Prod.fst ([] ++ [(A ++ (descWord kd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c')]), q ≠ A ++ (u ++ { index := kd } :: (v ++ ({ index := k } :: descWord kd j₁ ++ (descWord kd j₂ ++ S))))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The bystander is not any word the pass's transport visits. Each such word starts, after A, with a letter of the run above k, and every one of those is more than one above σ_kd.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.loopTwo {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ j₂ e ed : Fin n} (hed : ↑ed + 1 = ↑e) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑ed) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑e) (hji : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑i) (S : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c c' : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (m : ℕ) (k kd : Fin n) (A Y : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ↑kd + 1 = ↑k → ↑k = ↑e + m → ↑k ≤ ↑i → (∀ y ∈ Y, ↑kd + 1 < ↑y.index) → descWord i j₁ = Y ++ { index := k } :: descWord kd j₁ → MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(A ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k j₂ ++ S)), c), (A ++ (descWord kd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c')]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(A ++ (descWord kd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c), (A ++ (descWord kd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c')])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The loop, with the S-polynomial's other term riding along. Same walk as loop, but the element carries a second term throughout — the word the loop is heading for, which is what the corner's two reductions meet at. Because the bystander does not move (see above), it is one fixed word and the two distinctness obligations of each pass are discharged uniformly by pass_hne and pass_hcol.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.loopTwoFromTop {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ j₂ e ed idd : Fin n} (m : ℕ) (hed : ↑ed + 1 = ↑e) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑ed) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑e) (hid : ↑idd + 1 = ↑i) (hm : ↑i = ↑e + m) (A S : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c c' : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(A ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord i j₂ ++ S)), c), (A ++ (descWord idd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c')]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(A ++ (descWord idd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c), (A ++ (descWord idd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c')])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            loopTwo entered at the top, where Y is empty. This is the shape in which each of the corner's two terms is actually reduced: A is what already sits to the left of the long run, S what trails it (empty for the first term, [σᵢ] for the second), and the second listed term is the word they meet at.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.loopListSources {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ j₂ e ed : Fin n} (hed : ↑ed + 1 = ↑e) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑ed) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑e) (S : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (m : ℕ) (k kd : Fin n) (A Y : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ↑kd + 1 = ↑k → ↑k = ↑e + m → (∀ P ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), ∀ (D Y' : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (k' kd' : Fin n), P ≠ A ++ (D ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k' j₂ ++ S))) ∧ ∀ (u v : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), u ++ v = Y' → u ≠ [] → P ≠ A ++ (D ++ (u ++ { index := kd' } :: (v ++ ({ index := k' } :: descWord kd' j₁ ++ (descWord kd' j₂ ++ S)))))) → (∀ y ∈ Y, ↑kd + 1 < ↑y.index) → descWord i j₁ = Y ++ { index := k } :: descWord kd j₁ → MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (A ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k j₂ ++ S)), c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (A ++ (descWord kd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The loop against an arbitrary term list, with the source-only collision hypothesis.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Two generalisations of loopTwo at once, both forced by the corner.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Source-only collisions. loopTwoGen below asks that the parked word P be no extension of A at all. That is sufficient — every word any pass rewrites does have the form A ++ z — but not necessary, and hecke_prefix_head_separation.py measures where the difference bites: at 2a steps of the corner's closing phase no choice of left context satisfies it, while every source in the chain is unique, so the precise condition holds throughout.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            What the loop actually needs is that each parked word differ from the two families blockStep asks about, at every level. The accumulator only ever grows on the right of A, so quantifying over that growth D makes the hypothesis closed under the recursion: descending a level replaces D by σ_kd :: D.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            An arbitrary term list. blockStep has taken general L₁/L₂ all along; loopTwo and its descendants fixed them to [(P, c')] and [], which puts the parked term first. ofTerms is a representation rather than a normal form, so that choice is not free: a chain ending at [(P, c'), (w, c)] does not compose with one starting at [(w, c), (P, c')], even though the two are the same element. Carrying L₁ and L₂ through the induction removes the choice, and loopTwoGenSources / loopTwoGenRightSources are the two slots. The corner's opening phase needs both: the U-side loop parks V and the V-side loop parks U.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.loopTwoGenSources {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ j₂ e ed : Fin n} (hed : ↑ed + 1 = ↑e) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑ed) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑e) (S P : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c c' : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (m : ℕ) (k kd : Fin n) (A Y : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ↑kd + 1 = ↑k → ↑k = ↑e + m → (∀ (D Y' : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (k' kd' : Fin n), P ≠ A ++ (D ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k' j₂ ++ S))) ∧ ∀ (u v : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), u ++ v = Y' → u ≠ [] → P ≠ A ++ (D ++ (u ++ { index := kd' } :: (v ++ ({ index := k' } :: descWord kd' j₁ ++ (descWord kd' j₂ ++ S)))))) → (∀ y ∈ Y, ↑kd + 1 < ↑y.index) → descWord i j₁ = Y ++ { index := k } :: descWord kd j₁ → MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(P, c'), (A ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k j₂ ++ S)), c)]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(P, c'), (A ++ (descWord kd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c)])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The loop with the parked term listed first, the shape loopTwoGen and the a > b corner use. loopListSources at L₁ = [(P, c')], L₂ = [].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.loopTwoGenRightSources {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ j₂ e ed : Fin n} (hed : ↑ed + 1 = ↑e) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑ed) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑e) (S P : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c c' : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (m : ℕ) (k kd : Fin n) (A Y : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ↑kd + 1 = ↑k → ↑k = ↑e + m → (∀ (D Y' : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (k' kd' : Fin n), P ≠ A ++ (D ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k' j₂ ++ S))) ∧ ∀ (u v : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), u ++ v = Y' → u ≠ [] → P ≠ A ++ (D ++ (u ++ { index := kd' } :: (v ++ ({ index := k' } :: descWord kd' j₁ ++ (descWord kd' j₂ ++ S)))))) → (∀ y ∈ Y, ↑kd + 1 < ↑y.index) → descWord i j₁ = Y ++ { index := k } :: descWord kd j₁ → MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(A ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k j₂ ++ S)), c), (P, c')]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(A ++ (descWord kd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c), (P, c')])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The loop with the parked term listed second. loopListSources at L₁ = [], L₂ = [(P, c')].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            AlgElement.ofTerms is a representation, not a normal form: the same element with its two terms in the other order is a different value, so this does not follow from loopTwoGenSources by rearrangement — it has to be the same induction against the other slot of blockStep's term list, which is what loopListSources supplies.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The corner's opening phase needs exactly this. loopTwoGen forces the parked term first, so the U-side loop ends at [(V2, 1), (U0L, −1)]; the V-side loop that follows then has the V term active with the U term parked, and its source must therefore list the U term first. Without this variant the two loops do not compose without a change-of-representation argument.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.loopTwoGenRight {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ j₂ e ed : Fin n} (hed : ↑ed + 1 = ↑e) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑ed) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑e) (S P : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c c' : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (m : ℕ) (k kd : Fin n) (A Y : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ↑kd + 1 = ↑k → ↑k = ↑e + m → (∀ (z : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), P ≠ A ++ z) → (∀ y ∈ Y, ↑kd + 1 < ↑y.index) → descWord i j₁ = Y ++ { index := k } :: descWord kd j₁ → MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(A ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k j₂ ++ S)), c), (P, c')]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(A ++ (descWord kd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c), (P, c')])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            loopTwoGenRightSources with the sufficient collision hypothesis, matching loopTwoGen.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerBlock.loopTwoGen {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ j₂ e ed : Fin n} (hed : ↑ed + 1 = ↑e) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑ed) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑e) (S P : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c c' : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (m : ℕ) (k kd : Fin n) (A Y : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            ↑kd + 1 = ↑k → ↑k = ↑e + m → (∀ (z : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), P ≠ A ++ z) → (∀ y ∈ Y, ↑kd + 1 < ↑y.index) → descWord i j₁ = Y ++ { index := k } :: descWord kd j₁ → MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(P, c'), (A ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord k j₂ ++ S)), c)]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(P, c'), (A ++ (descWord kd ed ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord ed j₂ ++ S))), c)])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The loop with a parked term that is not its endpoint.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            loopTwo carries the word the loop is heading for. The corner needs the other arrangement too: while one term of the S-polynomial runs its loop, the other sits parked at a word of its own. Every word any pass rewrites has the form A ++ z — the accumulator only ever grows on the right of A — so a single hypothesis, that the parked word is not of that form, discharges every obligation of every pass at once. In the corner it holds for the cheapest of reasons: the two terms start with different letters.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            §4ag The a > b corner at every pair of depths #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            §4ad and §4ae close the columns b = 2 and b = 3 one at a time. §4af replaces the quadratic middle of any such column by a loop. What is left is the ends, and they are the same four steps whatever the depths are. This section assembles them.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The chain runs in three phases, in the order the confluence engine takes them:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • two setup steps carry the first term from the S-polynomial to the loop's entry shape, with the second term parked at U0;
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • the second term's whole reduction — its loop, then a Bokut–Shiao step at top i and the fixed-depth one at (i−2, i−1, j₂−1) — with the first term parked at V2;
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            • the first term's loop, with the second parked at the word they meet at.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Only the middle of each phase depends on the depths, and that is exactly what §4af's loop absorbs. Writing ed for j₂ − 1, the meeting word is σᵢ₋₂ ++ descWord (i−1) ed ++ descWord i j₁.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        (T6 i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ ed).isZero

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerGeneral.chain {n : ℕ} {i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ ed : Fin n} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i) (h₂ : ↑i₂ + 1 = ↑i₁) (hed : ↑ed + 1 = ↑j₂) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑ed) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑i₂) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (T0 i i₁ j₁ j₂) (T6 i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ ed)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The whole chain. Two setup steps, the second term's loop, its two closing steps, then the first term's loop — and the two terms coincide.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        noncomputable def UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerGeneral.oc {n : ℕ} (i i₁ j₁ j₂ : Fin n) (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑i₁) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑i₁) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        OverlapComposition (HeckeGen n) ℝ (heckeOrder n)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        The composition: the Bokut–Shiao rule at the deeper bottom j₁ against the one at j₂, overlapping in the trailing σᵢ.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerGeneral.oc_spoly_coeff {n : ℕ} {i i₁ j₁ j₂ : Fin n} (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑i₁) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑i₁) (m : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          (oc i i₁ j₁ j₂ h₁ hj₁ hj₂).spoly.coeff m = (T0 i i₁ j₁ j₂).coeff m

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The S-polynomial is V0 − U0. The two leading words cancel because the short run splits as descWord i j₂ = σᵢ :: descWord (i−1) j₂, which is exactly the overlap.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          This is regime-independent, and that is worth stating. Neither oc nor this identity relates j₁ to j₂ — both ask only j₁ ≤ i₁ and j₂ ≤ i₁. So the overlap composition and its S-polynomial are already established for the a ≤ b regime (j₂ ≤ j₁), diagonal j₂ = j₁ included, and not only for the a > b regime this namespace's chain and resolves go on to close. What is regime-specific is the reduction chain from T0 to zero, nothing before it.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Recorded because the a ≤ b arc (bean qou-auq3) had been carrying "OverlapComposition + spoly" on its open list, which was wrong: both were in the corpus, generic in both depths, the whole time. Verified by instantiating this lemma at j₂ ≤ j₁ and at j₂ = j₁.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerGeneral.resolves {n : ℕ} (hp : HeckeParams) {i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ ed : Fin n} (hn : 0 < n) (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i) (h₂ : ↑i₂ + 1 = ↑i₁) (hed : ↑ed + 1 = ↑j₂) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑ed) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑i₂) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          ∃ (nf : AlgElement (HeckeGen n) ℝ), ReducesToNF (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (oc i i₁ j₁ j₂ h₁ ⋯ ⋯).spoly nf ∧ nf.isZero

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The a > b corner, at every pair of depths. The Bokut–Shiao rule at bottom j₁ composed with the one at bottom j₂, whenever j₁ < j₂ ≤ i − 2, reduces to zero. No bound on either depth, and the chain's length — quadratic in them — is carried entirely by §4af's loop.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          §4am The a ≤ b tail, assembled — and why the order is not the engine's #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Everything the tail needs has been in the file since §4al: two blockPass applications, two Bokut–Shiao steps, and the two descWord splittings that make the terms meet. What was missing is the schedule, and it is not the engine's.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          hecke_tail_collision_check.py measured blockPass's collision hypothesis hpark — no other term is any extension of the block's left context — at both applications, under the order the confluence engine produces (block 1, the two Bokut–Shiao steps, block 2). It holds at the first and fails at the second, 8/8 off the diagonal. It fails for one reason: that block's last step emits the bystander, and that emission is the cancellation which ends the chain.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The reflex is to weaken hpark — to propagate down the source-only relaxation farComm_transport_right_sources already carries, since SingleStepReduction reads f.coeff (a ++ lm ++ b) off the source side and a collision on a word the block only ever produces costs nothing. That is three lemmas restated, and the relaxed proof would then owe an argument that a block's destination differs from each of its own intermediate sources.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          None of it is needed. The tail's two blocks act on different terms, so their steps commute, and MultiStepReduction fixes no order beyond each step's redex being present. Deg-lex runs block 1 first; that is the engine's scheduling accident, not a constraint on the Lean. Run block 2 first and its bystander is term 1 in its pre-block form, which does not extend σ_{i−2} :: A at all — and by the time term 1 moves, term 2 sits at a word beginning σ_{i−2}, which does not extend A. hecke_tail_reorder_check.py measures both, together with every source being unique and the chain still reaching zero, 8/8.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The last step lands on the bystander, and that is legal: monicStep constrains its source (hne), never its target. The landing is the cancellation, and the two terms then differ only in sign — the a > b regime's own ending, where chain stops at T6 and T6_isZero finishes the job.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The two words meet because of two splittings of one descending run, nothing more:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          descWord id j₂ = descWord id jpp ++ descWord jp j₂
descWord i  jp = descWord i jppp ++ descWord jpp jp

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          both instances of descWord_split.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          SingleStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (W, c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (W', c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          { index := x } ≠ { index := y }

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.tailChain {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i id idd j₂ jm j₁ jp jpp jppp : Fin n} (hid : ↑id + 1 = ↑i) (hidd : ↑idd + 1 = ↑id) (hjm : ↑jm + 1 = ↑j₁) (hjp : ↑j₁ + 1 = ↑jp) (hjpp : ↑jp + 1 = ↑jpp) (hjppp : ↑jpp + 1 = ↑jppp) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑jm) (hjppid : ↑jpp ≤ ↑id) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [({ index := idd } :: (descWord id jpp ++ (descWord i jppp ++ ([{ index := jp }, { index := jpp }, { index := j₁ }] ++ { index := jp } :: descWord jm j₂))), c), (descWord id jpp ++ (descWord i jppp ++ ([{ index := jp }, { index := jpp }, { index := j₁ }] ++ { index := jp } :: (descWord jm j₂ ++ [{ index := i }]))), -c)]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [({ index := idd } :: (descWord id jpp ++ (descWord jp j₂ ++ (descWord i jppp ++ descWord jpp jp))), c), ({ index := idd } :: (descWord id jpp ++ (descWord jp j₂ ++ (descWord i jppp ++ descWord jpp jp))), -c)])
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.tailChain_indices_nonvacuous :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          ∃ (i : Fin 13) (id : Fin 13) (idd : Fin 13) (j₂ : Fin 13) (jm : Fin 13) (j₁ : Fin 13) (jp : Fin 13) (jpp : Fin 13) (jppp : Fin 13), ↑id + 1 = ↑i ∧ ↑idd + 1 = ↑id ∧ ↑jm + 1 = ↑j₁ ∧ ↑j₁ + 1 = ↑jp ∧ ↑jp + 1 = ↑jpp ∧ ↑jpp + 1 = ↑jppp ∧ ↑j₂ ≤ ↑jm ∧ ↑jpp ≤ ↑id

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The tail's index hypotheses are satisfiable, so tailChain is not vacuous. These are a = 4, b = 6 at n = 13 — the case the probes measure.
