                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.tailChainFromTwo {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i id idd j₂ j₁ jp jpp jppp : Fin n} (hid : ↑id + 1 = ↑i) (hidd : ↑idd + 1 = ↑id) (hjp : ↑j₁ + 1 = ↑jp) (hjpp : ↑jp + 1 = ↑jpp) (hjppp : ↑jpp + 1 = ↑jppp) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑j₁) (hjppid : ↑jpp ≤ ↑id) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [({ index := idd } :: (descWord id jpp ++ (descWord i jppp ++ ([{ index := jp }] ++ { index := jpp } :: (descWord j₁ j₂ ++ [{ index := jp }])))), c), (descWord id jpp ++ (descWord i jppp ++ ([{ index := jp }] ++ { index := jpp } :: (descWord j₁ j₂ ++ ([{ index := jp }] ++ [{ index := i }])))), -c)]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [({ index := idd } :: (descWord id jpp ++ (descWord jp j₂ ++ (descWord i jppp ++ descWord jpp jp))), c), ({ index := idd } :: (descWord id jpp ++ (descWord jp j₂ ++ (descWord i jppp ++ descWord jpp jp))), -c)])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The tail from the block's second level on — the diagonal included.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          tailChain above asks j₂ ≤ jm, so it is off-diagonal only. This asks j₂ ≤ j₁, and at b = a the two coincide: the same relation blockPass and blockPassFromTwo stand in, one level up.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Neither statement subsumes the other, because their sources differ. On the diagonal the block is one level shorter and blockPassFromTwo's source word is not blockPass's — the trailing σ_jp sits on the other side of the descending run, one transport later. So this is not tailChain with a weakened hypothesis; it is the same four-step argument starting from the later word.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Everything after the two blocks is identical to tailChain's, and measurement says so rather than inspection: hecke_tail_diagonal_check.py finds the diagonal's two Bokut–Shiao steps and its endpoint word to be the same as the off-diagonal's, with only the block source differing — and finds the same collision pattern, hpark failing under the engine's order at the second block and holding under the reordered one, 4/4 at a = b = 3..6.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.tailChainFromTwo_covers_diagonal :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          ∃ (i : Fin 11) (id : Fin 11) (idd : Fin 11) (j₂ : Fin 11) (j₁ : Fin 11) (jp : Fin 11) (jpp : Fin 11) (jppp : Fin 11), ↑id + 1 = ↑i ∧ ↑idd + 1 = ↑id ∧ ↑j₁ + 1 = ↑jp ∧ ↑jp + 1 = ↑jpp ∧ ↑jpp + 1 = ↑jppp ∧ ↑j₂ = ↑j₁ ∧ ↑jpp ≤ ↑id

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The diagonal b = a is inside tailChainFromTwo's reach: j₂ = j₁.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          §4an The a ≤ b chain's opening — most of it was already proved #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Two facts about CornerGeneral, both established by instantiation rather than by reading a signature, and both of which shrink the a ≤ b arc's open list.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The overlap and the S-polynomial were never regime-specific. Neither CornerGeneral.oc nor oc_spoly_coeff relates j₁ to j₂ — see the note on that lemma. So the a ≤ b corner starts from the same T0, diagonal included, and hecke_prefix_loop_fit.py's companion measurement confirms it against the engine: the start element is exactly ofTerms [(V0, 1), (U0, −1)].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The first two steps were not either. s1 and s2 ask only i₁+1 = i, i₂+1 = i₁ and j₁ ≤ i₂ — Lean's unused-variable linter reports j₂ unused when they are instantiated, which is the sharpest possible statement of it. So they carry the a ≤ b chain to ofTerms [(V2, 1), (U0, −1)] unchanged, and that is exactly where the engine's own replay puts it after two steps.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          What this namespace adds is the second term's head, which the a > b regime does not share: there s3/s4 need hed : ed+1 = j₂ with j₁ ≤ ed, i.e. j₁ < j₂, and cannot be instantiated here at all.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          uHead is that head — and it is loopTwoGen at m = 0, not new work. I first proved it by hand before checking; the instantiation is k = i₁, kd = ed = i₂, A = [σᵢ₋₁], S = [σᵢ], Y = [σᵢ], and the hypothesis descWord i j₁ = Y ++ (σ_k :: descWord kd j₁) is just the run's first two letters peeled off. Recorded because the consequence matters for the assembly: if one level is loopTwoGen at m = 0, the whole U-side loop is loopTwoGen at general m, so the opening phase's second lineage is a single application rather than a chain.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          It is the same two-rule motif as s1/s2 — a Bokut–Shiao step then a far-commutation — displaced one letter right, because U0 carries a leading σᵢ₋₁ that V0 does not:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          U0  = σᵢ₋₁ · σᵢ · (descWord i₁ j₁ ++ [σᵢ₋₁]) · descWord i₂ j₂ · σᵢ
  B →  σᵢ₋₁ · σᵢ · (σᵢ₋₂ σᵢ₋₁ descWord i₂ j₁) · descWord i₂ j₂ · σᵢ
  F →  σᵢ₋₁ · σᵢ₋₂ · σᵢ · σᵢ₋₁ · descWord i₂ j₁ · descWord i₂ j₂ · σᵢ

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The Bokut–Shiao redex straddles the two descending runs — it is descWord i₁ j₁ ++ [σᵢ₋₁], whose last letter is descWord i₁ j₂'s first — and the far-commutation then moves σᵢ right past σᵢ₋₂, which is legal because i₂ + 1 < i. Both collision hypotheses are discharged by one letter: the bystander V2 opens σᵢ₋₂ and every word here opens σᵢ₋₁. That is the opening phase's head separation, which hecke_prefix_head_separation.py measures to hold for the first a²−3a+9 steps and to fail thereafter.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerLe.uLoop {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ jpp jppp : Fin n} (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i) (h₂ : ↑i₂ + 1 = ↑i₁) (hjpp : ↑jpp + 1 = ↑jppp) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑jpp) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑jppp) (htop : ↑jppp ≤ ↑i₁) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(CornerGeneral.V2 i i₂ j₁ j₂, 1), (CornerGeneral.U0 i i₁ j₁ j₂, -1)]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(CornerGeneral.V2 i i₂ j₁ j₂, 1), (U0L i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ jpp, -1)])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              The second term's whole loop, at general depth. loopTwoGen at m = i₁ − jppp, which hecke_opening_coverage.py measures as the U side's entire contribution to the opening phase — 2, 5, 9 steps at a = 4, 5, 6.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              uHead below is this at jppp = i₁, i.e. m = 0, i.e. a = 4. That the general case is the same lemma at a larger m is why the opening phase's second lineage is one application rather than a chain of levels.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerLe.vLoop {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ jpp jppp : Fin n} (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i) (h₂ : ↑i₂ + 1 = ↑i₁) (hjpp : ↑jpp + 1 = ↑jppp) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑jpp) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑jppp) (htop : ↑jppp ≤ ↑i) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(CornerGeneral.V2 i i₂ j₁ j₂, 1), (U0L i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ jpp, -1)]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(V2L i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ jpp, 1), (U0L i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ jpp, -1)])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The first term's whole loop, at general depth, with the second parked at the word its own loop left it on.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                V2 is already in the loop's entry shape on the nose — [σᵢ₋₂] ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord i j₂ ++ [])) — so this is loopTwoGenRight at A = [σᵢ₋₂], k = i, S = [], and m = i − jppp. That is one more than uLoop's m = i₁ − jppp, which is why hecke_opening_coverage.py measures the two lineages at L and L + 1 steps for the same bottom jppp.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The two loops compose without any change of representation, and that is what loopTwoGenRight bought: uLoop runs loopTwoGen, which lists the parked term first, so it ends at [(V2, 1), (U0L, −1)] — V parked, U active. Here V is the active one and U the parked one, so the source must list V first, which is the same list. The collision hypothesis is one letter: U0L opens σᵢ₋₁, and every word this loop touches extends [σᵢ₋₂].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerLe.trio {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {j₂ jm j₁ jp jpp : Fin n} (hjm : ↑jm + 1 = ↑j₁) (hjp : ↑j₁ + 1 = ↑jp) (hjpp : ↑jp + 1 = ↑jpp) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑j₁) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (A T : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (hpark : ∀ r ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), ∀ (z : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), r ≠ A ++ z) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (A ++ (bsWord₁ jpp j₁ ++ (descWord jp j₂ ++ T)), c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (A ++ ([{ index := jp }, { index := jpp }] ++ ([{ index := j₁ }, { index := jp }] ++ { index := j₁ } :: (descWord jm j₂ ++ T))), c * (hp.q - hp.q⁻¹)) :: (A ++ ([{ index := jp }, { index := jpp }] ++ ([{ index := j₁ }, { index := jp }] ++ (descWord jm j₂ ++ T))), c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The trio: one Bokut–Shiao step then quadPair, in the shape both lineages of the opening phase use.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                hecke_opening_trio_shape.py measures the six steps after TL as B(jp,jpp,j₁), Y(j₁,jp), Q(j₁) twice, 6/6 — and the two occurrences differ only in A and T, so this is one lemma applied twice rather than a U trio and a V trio:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A T
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                U [σᵢ₋₁] ++ descWord i₂ jpp ++ descWord i jppp [σᵢ]
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                V [σᵢ₋₂] ++ descWord i₁ jpp ++ descWord i jppp []

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The Bokut–Shiao redex straddles the two descending runs: descWord i j₁ splits at jppp, leaving descWord jpp j₁, and descWord jpp j₂ opens with σ_jpp — so descWord jpp j₁ ++ [σ_jpp] is bsWord₁ jpp j₁, sitting on the join. Its image bsWord₂ jp jpp j₁ = [σ_jp, σ_jpp, σ_jp, σ_j₁] then meets descWord jp j₂, whose first two letters are σ_jp, σ_j₁ — and σ_jp σ_j₁ σ_jp followed by σ_j₁ is exactly quadPair's redex. Neither step creates it alone, which is the same mechanism §4al describes one level down.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                hj₂ : j₂ ≤ j₁ is the regime. It is what makes descWord jp j₂ open with those two letters, and it is b ≥ a — so this lemma does not instantiate in the a > b corner at all. The diagonal b = a is included: there descWord j₁ j₂ is the single letter σ_j₁ and descWord jm j₂ is empty.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                One collision hypothesis serves both steps: no bystander extends A. quadPair asks about A ++ [σ_jp, σ_jpp], which is an extension of A, and bsStep asks about a source that begins with A. At both call sites it is discharged by a single letter — the U trio's A opens σᵢ₋₁ against the parked V2L's σᵢ₋₂, and the V trio's the other way round.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                AlgElement (HeckeGen n) ℝ

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerLe.openingLoops {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ jpp jppp : Fin n} (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i) (h₂ : ↑i₂ + 1 = ↑i₁) (hjpp : ↑jpp + 1 = ↑jppp) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑jpp) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑jppp) (htop : ↑jppp ≤ ↑i₁) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (CornerGeneral.T0 i i₁ j₁ j₂) (TL i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ jpp)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The a ≤ b chain's opening phase, loops included — the two setup steps and both loops, in the one order in which they compose.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  hecke_opening_coverage.py decomposes the opening's a² − 3a + 9 steps into five stretches: the two setup steps, the U loop (L steps), a trio, the V loop (L + 1 steps), and a second trio. This lemma is the first three of those five — 2 + L + (L + 1) = 2L + 3 steps — because both loops must precede both trios, and that ordering is a constraint, not a preference.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  L = (a² − 3a)/2: measured 2, 5, 9 at a = 4, 5, 6, so 2L + 9 recovers the phase length 13, 19, 27. It is not jpp − j₁, which this docstring said until hecke_opening_trio_shape.py measured it — that difference is 2 for every a, and agrees only at a = 4. The loop's level parameter m = a − 4 is the thing that is linear in a; its step count is not, because each level descends by a pass whose own length grows.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  The probe measures why. loopTwoGenRight (like every loop lemma here) is stated for a two-term element, while quadPair, which the trios use, takes general L₁/L₂. Under the order the confluence engine itself produces, the U trio's quadratic step splits U into two terms before the V loop has run — at step 6, 9 and 13 for a = 4, 5, 6, against V-loop completion at 9, 15 and 23 — so a V loop scheduled after the U trio would face three terms and no loop lemma applies. Running both loops first keeps the element at two terms throughout, and the trios then run against the general-list quadPair.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  That the reordering is legal is the same argument §4am makes for the tail: the two lineages act on different terms, so their steps commute, and MultiStepReduction fixes no order beyond each step's redex being present. Deg-lex picks one; the Lean is not obliged to.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Monomial (HeckeGen n)

U takes (x, y) = (i₁, i₂), V takes (i₂, i₁).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerLe.lineage_eq_trio_source {n : ℕ} {i x y j₁ j₂ jp jpp jppp : Fin n} (hjpp : ↑jp + 1 = ↑jpp) (hjppp : ↑jpp + 1 = ↑jppp) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑jpp) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑jpp) (htop : ↑jppp ≤ ↑i) (T : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    [{ index := x }] ++ (descWord y jpp ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord jpp j₂ ++ T))) = trioLeft i x y jpp jppp ++ (bsWord₁ jpp j₁ ++ (descWord jp j₂ ++ T))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Both lineage words open on the trio's redex. descWord i j₁ splits at jppp, and descWord jpp j₂ opens with σ_jpp; the two halves meet as bsWord₁ jpp j₁. This is the one rewriting that turns U0L and V2L into trio's source shape, and it is the same for both.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerLe.openingPhase_of_loops {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ jm jp jpp jppp : Fin n} (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i) (h₂ : ↑i₂ + 1 = ↑i₁) (hjm : ↑jm + 1 = ↑j₁) (hjp : ↑j₁ + 1 = ↑jp) (hjpp : ↑jp + 1 = ↑jpp) (hjppp : ↑jpp + 1 = ↑jppp) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑j₁) (htopi : ↑jppp ≤ ↑i) (hloops : MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (CornerGeneral.T0 i i₁ j₁ j₂) (TL i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ jpp)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (CornerGeneral.T0 i i₁ j₁ j₂) (TOpen i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ jm jp jpp jppp (hp.q - hp.q⁻¹))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The a ≤ b chain's opening phase, whole — a² − 3a + 9 steps, from the S-polynomial T0 to the four-term TOpen.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Five stretches, in the one order in which the lemmas compose: s1, s2, the U loop, the V loop, then trio twice. hecke_opening_trio_shape.py measures 2 + L + (L+1) + 6 = 2L + 9 steps and 2L + 9 = a² − 3a + 9, so this is the whole phase and nothing is left over.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The two trios run U before V, which is deg-lex's order and also the one the term list forces: openingLoops ends at [(V2L, 1), (U0L, −1)], so U is the second entry and V the parked one; after U's quadratic step splits it in two, V is the first entry of three. Each trio's collision hypothesis is one letter — U's left context opens σᵢ₋₁ against the parked V2L's σᵢ₋₂, and V's the other way round against both of U's outputs, which share U's prefix.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The closing phase's F-run #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      hecke_closing_from_topen.py measures the 4(a−1) steps after TOpen as one shape, uniform in a and b: an F-run of 2a−3 steps, two Bokut–Shiao steps, the same F-run again, then the cancellation. Machine-checked — exactly two adjacent B steps, the two runs literally equal.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The engine interleaves two letters through the run, but they are on one term, so the order is free and the run sequences into three lemma calls. The first is the bare far-commutation σ_jpp σ_j₁ → σ_j₁ σ_jpp, which makes σ_jp and σ_j₁ adjacent; the pair then transports left past descWord i jppp — first σ_jp, whose every obstacle is ≥ jppp = jp + 1… no: ≥ jppp, and jp + 1 = jpp < jppp, so all far-commute; then σ_j₁, for which they are ≥ jppp = j₁ + 3. That is 2(a−2) engine steps replaced by two inductions.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The A-prefix collision hypothesis is unavailable here, and this is the 2a hard core. The two terms of one lineage share their whole left context — quadPair splits a word into two that differ only in an interior σ_j₁ — so "no other term extends A" is false at exactly the 2a steps hecke_prefix_head_separation.py counted. Measured again at TOpen: U1 extends Uh's A. What the steps actually need is monicStep's hne and the transports' split-indexed source condition, which this arc's _sources relaxations supply — so the hypotheses below are stated in that form and not collapsed.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerLe.fRun_gen {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ jp jpp : Fin n} (hjp : ↑j₁ + 1 = ↑jp) (hjpp : ↑jp + 1 = ↑jpp) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (A S D : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (hD : ∀ y ∈ D, ↑jpp < ↑y.index) (hclose : D ++ [{ index := jpp }, { index := jp }] = descWord i jp) (hne : ∀ q ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), q ≠ A ++ (D ++ ([{ index := jp }, { index := jpp }, { index := j₁ }, { index := jp }] ++ S))) (hcol₁ : ∀ (u v : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), u ++ v = D → u ≠ [] → ∀ r ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), r ≠ A ++ (u ++ { index := jp } :: (v ++ ([{ index := j₁ }, { index := jpp }, { index := jp }] ++ S)))) (hcol₂ : ∀ (u v : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), u ++ v = D → u ≠ [] → ∀ r ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), r ≠ A ++ [{ index := jp }] ++ (u ++ { index := j₁ } :: (v ++ ([{ index := jpp }, { index := jp }] ++ S)))) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (A ++ (D ++ ([{ index := jp }, { index := jpp }, { index := j₁ }, { index := jp }] ++ S)), c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (A ++ ([{ index := jp }, { index := j₁ }] ++ (descWord i jp ++ S)), c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The F-run over an arbitrary run D. fRun below is this at D = descWord i jppp, which is the only shape the a ≥ 3 closing phase needs.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Two hypotheses replace fRun's jppp ≤ i, and neither mentions jppp. hD is what the two transports actually ask of the run — every letter far enough above j₁ and jp to commute — and hclose is what descWord_split was being used to produce. So the run may be empty, which is the a = 2 corner: there jpp = i, descWord i jppp is empty, and jppp ≤ i is false while the run still closes up ([] ++ [σ_jpp, σ_jp] is descWord i jp on the nose).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Same split as fRun_target_eq_of_left one section down — take the list identity as a hypothesis, keep the descWord_split supplier as the named corollary.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (A ++ (descWord i jppp ++ ([{ index := jp }, { index := jpp }, { index := j₁ }, { index := jp }] ++ S)), c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (A ++ ([{ index := jp }, { index := j₁ }] ++ (descWord i jp ++ S)), c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The closing phase's F-run, as three lemma calls rather than 2a−3 steps. S is whatever trails the block: σ_j₁ :: R for the h-weighted term of a lineage and R for the plain one, which is the only difference between them.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      fRun_gen at D = descWord i jppp; htop enters only through the run's close-up, which is why the a = 2 corner can use the general form.
