                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The a = 1 S-polynomial resolves. The six entries the tail lands on annihilate in three pairs — two split, one adjacent — so the element is zero.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The join is the one #5586 built: prefixChain₁ to TCancel₁, TCancel₁_coeffEq to drop the cancelling pair it already carries, then the tail, absorbed through MultiStepReduction.congr_source.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          §4ao The other corner: a > b #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          CornerLe proves the a ≤ b prefix for every a. This namespace is the corner on the other side of the diagonal, j₁ < j₂.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          It is strictly easier, which is not what "the other corner" suggests. hecke_agtb_corner_shape.py and hecke_agtb_lineage_schedule.py measure it across 15 cases:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • the S-polynomial reduces completely to zero — CornerLe's prefix ends at a partial cancellation with two terms surviving; here nothing is left;
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • the element never exceeds two terms, because the chain uses no quadratic step. quadStep is the only rule that splits one term in two, so quadPair, trio, TOpen and ofTerms_cancel_split — the whole four-term apparatus CornerLe needed — are unnecessary here;
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • the step count is b² + 3b + 5, with no a-dependence at all;
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          • every step is a bsStep or a far-commutation. Measured 16/16: each step the engine's trace labels Y is bokutShiaoRelation x (x+1) x, which has the same leading word as Yang–Baxter and differs from it by a sign — the same coincidence §4al records for quadPair, one level down.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Both lineages therefore run without branching, and they meet on bsWord₂ i₂ i₁ (j₂−1) ++ descWord i j₁ — the same two-run shape as CornerLe.WStar with the bottoms swapped.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The block #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          hecke_agtb_lineage_schedule.py measures both lineages as a sequence of blocks, each one Bokut–Shiao step followed by a run of far-commutations — and 69/77 of those runs move a single letter past contiguously-descending obstacles, so each run is one farComm_transport_left_sources call. A block therefore costs two lemma applications no matter how long its run is, which is why the chain is b² + 3b + 5 steps but only O(b) lemma calls.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The eight exceptions are exactly the a = b + 1 cases, where the last block interleaves two moved letters. That is where this general form stops and a special case begins — the same shape as CornerLe's a = 3 and a = 2.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerGt.gtBlock {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {j₁ x x' : Fin n} (hx : ↑x + 1 = ↑x') (hj : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑x) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (A w B : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (hw : ∀ y ∈ w, ↑x + 1 < ↑y.index) (hne : ∀ q ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), q ≠ A ++ w ++ bsWord₁ x' j₁ ++ B) (hcol : ∀ (u v : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), u ++ v = w → u ≠ [] → ∀ r ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), r ≠ A ++ (u ++ { index := x } :: (v ++ { index := x' } :: (descWord x j₁ ++ B)))) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (A ++ w ++ bsWord₁ x' j₁ ++ B, c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (A ++ { index := x } :: (w ++ { index := x' } :: (descWord x j₁ ++ B)), c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          One block. bsStep at (x, x+1, j₁), then the σₓ it emits transports left past w.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The two compose with nothing between them because bsWord₂ x x' j₁ opens with σₓ: the Bokut–Shiao step's output is the transport's input on the nose, with the run w sitting in the step's own left context.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerGt.gtRun {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i j₁ j₂ j₂' : Fin n} (hj₂' : ↑j₂' + 1 = ↑j₂) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑j₂') (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (a₀ : HeckeGen n) (hhead : ∀ q ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), ∀ (X : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), q ≠ a₀ :: X) (k : ℕ) (y z : Fin n) (A₀ w B : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          ↑y = ↑j₂ + k → ↑z + 1 = ↑y → w ++ descWord y j₁ = descWord i j₁ → (∀ u ∈ w, ↑y < ↑u.index) → MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (a₀ :: (A₀ ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ (descWord y j₂ ++ B))), c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (a₀ :: (A₀ ++ (descWord z j₂' ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ B))), c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The whole run, at any length — gtBlock iterated.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Each block pulls the leading letter of the trailing descending run across descWord i j₁, demotes it by one, and deposits it on the left. So the run descWord y j₂ slides down by one — to descWord z j₂' — and jumps to the left of descWord i j₁. k is the number of blocks minus one: the run has k + 1 letters.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          z and j₂' are the predecessors of y and j₂, passed as parameters with + 1 = hypotheses rather than constructed. That is this file's idiom for a Fin n predecessor (descWord_cons_le takes its i' the same way), and it is what keeps the induction free of Fin n arithmetic: the one place a predecessor must be built is the recursive call's z − 1.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          hsplit : w ++ descWord y j₁ = descWord i j₁ is what makes the block applicable — the redex bsWord₁ y j₁ is the tail of descWord i j₁ from y down, plus the run's leading letter. Carrying it as a hypothesis means no Fin n successor is ever needed for w, which is what a direct w = descWord i (y+1) would have forced.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          hj₁ : j₁ ≤ j₂' is the corner's own hypothesis a > b — the last block, which consumes σⱼ₂, needs floor room one below j₂.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Both lineages are this one lemma. The first at a₀ = σᵢ₋₂, A₀ = [σᵢ₋₁, σᵢ₋₂], w = descWord i i₁, y = i₂, B = []; the second at a₀ = σᵢ₋₁, A₀ = [], w = [σᵢ], y = i₁, B = [σᵢ].

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          b = 1: the base case, uniform in a #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          b = 1 means j₂ = i₁, which collapses descWord i₁ j₂ to the single letter σᵢ₋₁ in both S-polynomial terms. Nine steps — five on the first term, four on the second — and the count is independent of a, as it is for every b.

Same collapse on the other term: descWord i₁ j₂ is the single letter σᵢ₋₁.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerGt.vOpen {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i i₁ i₂ j₁ : Fin n} (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i) (h₂ : ↑i₂ + 1 = ↑i₁) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑i₂) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (S : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (hneI : ∀ q ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), ∀ (X : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), q ≠ { index := i } :: X) (hne2 : ∀ q ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), ∀ (X : Monomial (HeckeGen n)), q ≠ { index := i₂ } :: X) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ ([{ index := i₁ }, { index := i }, { index := i₁ }] ++ S), c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ ([{ index := i₂ }, { index := i₁ }, { index := i₂ }] ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ S), c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The first lineage's opening, for any b. Five steps, from descWord i j₁ ++ ([σᵢ₋₁, σᵢ, σᵢ₋₁] ++ S) to [σᵢ₋₂, σᵢ₋₁, σᵢ₋₂] ++ (descWord i j₁ ++ S), with S an arbitrary trailing context carried inert throughout.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          S is what makes this b-independent. The S-polynomial's first term is descWord i j₁ ++ (σᵢ₋₁ :: descWord i j₂), and descWord i j₂ splits as [σᵢ, σᵢ₋₁] ++ descWord i₂ j₂; the second factor never participates, so S = descWord i₂ j₂ and b = 1 is the case S = []. hecke_agtb_lineage_schedule.py measures that 10/10 — the words at every b ≥ 2 are the b = 1 words with exactly that suffix appended. (Its one exception, a = 3, b = 2, is a genuine index coincidence at the fifth step, recorded there; this lemma is stated for the general case and simply does not apply to it.)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Two hypotheses cover all five collisions, because the words this run touches open only two letters: σᵢ for the first two and σᵢ₋₂ for the last three. Neither mentions S, which is why the generalisation costs nothing.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          Monomial (HeckeGen n)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The word both lineages reach, where the element vanishes. This is bsWord₂ i₂ i₁ (j₂ − 1) ++ descWord i j₁ at j₂ = i₁, where j₂ − 1 is i₂ and descWord i₂ i₂ is a single letter.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerGt.sPolyChain_gt₁ {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i i₁ i₂ j₁ j₂ : Fin n} (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i) (h₂ : ↑i₂ + 1 = ↑i₁) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑i₂) (hj₂i₁ : j₂ = i₁) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (CornerGeneral.T0 i i₁ j₁ j₂) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(WGt₁ i i₁ i₂ j₁, 1), (WGt₁ i i₁ i₂ j₁, -1)])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The whole a > b chain at b = 1, nine steps, T0 to a two-term element whose entries are equal and oppositely signed.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Five steps on the first term, four on the second. Every step is a bsStep or a one-letter far-commutation σᵢ σᵢ₋₂ → σᵢ₋₂ σᵢ; there is no quadratic step, so neither term ever splits and no coefficient moves — the two terms keep the 1 and −1 they start with, which is what makes the meeting a cancellation.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The fourth step of the second lineage is bokutShiaoRelation i₂ i₁ i₂, whose bottom equals the pair's lower index. That is the rule the engine's trace names Y: it shares a leading word with Yang–Baxter and differs by a sign, so the monic Bokut–Shiao form is the one that applies — §4al makes the same move one level down for quadPair.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Every collision hypothesis is a head. The first lineage's words open σᵢ or σᵢ₋₂ and the second's open σᵢ₋₁; once the first has finished, the word it parks on opens σᵢ₋₂, still against σᵢ₋₁.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerGt.sPoly_zero_gt₁ {n : ℕ} (i i₁ i₂ j₁ : Fin n) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            (AlgElement.ofTerms [(WGt₁ i i₁ i₂ j₁, 1), (WGt₁ i i₁ i₂ j₁, -1)]).CoeffEq (AlgElement.ofTerms [])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The a > b S-polynomial resolves to zero at b = 1. The two entries sPolyChain_gt₁ lands on are the same word with opposite signs, so they contribute nothing and the element is zero.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            They are adjacent, which is why this is ofTerms_cancel_pair and not CornerLe's ofTerms_cancel_split: there, trio's quadratic step emits each lineage's h-weighted word immediately before its plain one, so the two cancelling entries are separated by two survivors. Here nothing splits, so nothing sits between them — and nothing survives.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            b = 2: one block on the first lineage, two on the second #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            b = 2 means j₂ = i₂, which makes descWord i j₂ three letters and descWord i₁ j₂ two. Fifteen steps — eight on the first term, seven on the second — which is b² + 3b + 5 at b = 2, and again independent of a.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The first lineage is vOpen at S = [σᵢ₋₂] followed by one gtBlock; the second is two gtBlocks followed by two bare bsSteps. That is the general shape hecke_agtb_lineage_schedule.py measures — b blocks per lineage plus two trailing B-only steps on the second — with the first lineage's opening block absorbed into vOpen, which is why only b − 1 of them appear there.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            The order below is not deg-lex's. At a = 3 — the a = b + 1 case, where descWord i₃ j₁ is a single letter — the engine's first-redex rule interleaves the last block's two moved letters differently, which is the exception the probe records. MultiStepReduction does not require deg-lex order, only that every step is applicable, so the schedule below covers a = 3 too: its hypothesis is j₁ ≤ i₃, i.e. a ≥ 3, with equality allowed.

Both halves are needed and neither is decoration: the reduction says the completion procedure reaches the element, and the coefficient equality says nothing is left when it gets there.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                §4as The corner against the criterion #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                IsGrobnerShirshovBasis.overlap_resolves asks, for each composition, for ∃ nf, ReducesToNF … oc.spoly nf ∧ nf.isZero. The five corner theorems give something one step short of that: a chain out of T0 ending coefficientwise zero. Three things close the gap, and all three were already in the file —

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • CornerGeneral.oc_spoly_coeff, which identifies oc.spoly with T0 and is regime-independent: it relates neither depth to the other, asking only j₁ ≤ i₁ and j₂ ≤ i₁;
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • reducesToZero_congr, which carries the obligation across that CoeffEq;
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • isNormalForm_of_isZero, since a zero element is trivially a normal form.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                So the only new content here is the case analysis: which of the five theorems applies at which depth, and the Fin n witnesses each needs.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.CornerCriterion.resolves_of_T0 {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i i₁ j₁ j₂ : Fin n} (h₁ : ↑i₁ + 1 = ↑i) (hj₁ : ↑j₁ ≤ ↑i₁) (hj₂ : ↑j₂ ≤ ↑i₁) (h : ∃ (E : AlgElement (HeckeGen n) ℝ), MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (CornerGeneral.T0 i i₁ j₁ j₂) E ∧ E.CoeffEq (AlgElement.ofTerms [])) :

Every corner theorem ends ∃ E, T0 →* E ∧ CoeffEq E 0; this is that, restated for oc.spoly.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Every Bokut–Shiao × Bokut–Shiao overlap at top i − 1 resolves.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The case analysis is on the two depths, and it is the only new content:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                j₁ < j₂ sPoly_gt_resolves — the a > b corner, uniform in a
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                j₂ ≤ j₁, j₁ = i₁ sPoly_le_resolves₁
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                j₂ ≤ j₁, j₁ + 1 = i₁ sPoly_le_resolves₂
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                j₂ ≤ j₁, j₁ + 2 = i₁ sPoly_le_resolves₃
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                j₂ ≤ j₁, j₁ + 3 ≤ i₁ sPoly_le_resolves

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                jm is j₁ − 1, and it does not always exist. Only the a ≥ 2 branches need it — the a = 1 branch and the whole a > b regime never mention it — so it is derived inside the proof, from hcov, rather than taken as a parameter. As a parameter it blocked j₁ = 0 outright, including the cases whose reduction chains already exist.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                hcov : 1 ≤ j₁ ∨ 1 ≤ j₂ ∨ i₁ = 0 is exactly the complement of the gap: its negation is j₁ = 0 ∧ j₂ = 0 ∧ i₁ ≥ 1. Each disjunct discharges the a ≥ 2 branch differently — the first directly; the second because j₂ ≤ j₁ holds there, so 1 ≤ j₂ gives 1 ≤ j₁; the third vacuously, since that branch also carries j₁ + 1 ≤ i₁, which i₁ = 0 contradicts.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                So what remains open is the deep diagonal j₁ = j₂ = 0 with i₁ ≥ 1 — not all of j₁ = 0, as this section previously said. j₁ = 0 with j₂ ≥ 1 is the a > b regime and was always covered; j₁ = j₂ = i₁ = 0 is the a = 1 branch and was too. That is a real gap, not a stylistic one, and the hypothesis is now stated so that its negation names the gap exactly.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                hq is needed only by the a = 1 branch, where the first term carries coefficient h and a SingleStepReduction needs it nonzero to transport.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                §4au The overlap of a proper composition is one letter #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Every composition namespace above is indexed by the shape of the composition rather than by the kinds of its two rules — CyclicQuad wants r.lm = u' ++ [σₓ], BraidSelfOverlap wants both rules on the braid word, BokutShiaoBraid wants rule₂ on it — and every single one of them fixes overlap to one letter. IsGrobnerShirshovBasis.overlap_resolves, by contrast, quantifies over every OverlapComposition. So the gap between that machinery and the criterion is exactly the multi-letter overlaps.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                §4m already answered this at n = 4, and this section was first written as though it had not — the correction is recorded here rather than quietly fixed. overlapTriples_four_proper_overlap_length_one decides it by kernel evaluation, and §4m's prose gives the reason in outline ("a suffix of length ≥ 2 ends low-then-high while every prefix of length ≥ 2 starts high-then-low"). What is new here is only that the fact holds for every n, by proof rather than by decide at one n; the invariant below is a machine-checked form of §4m's sketch. Read the two together, not as rivals.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                (The outline is a sketch and not literally the statement: σⱼσᵢσⱼ with j = i + 1 is not descending after its first letter, and σᵢσᵢ is neither strictly low-then-high nor strictly high-then-low — which is exactly why the quadratic self-pairing is a legal two-letter overlap shape, saved only by having an empty left context. The invariant used below, "the head is the maximum", has no such edge cases.)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Measured at more than one n first, in hecke_overlap_length_probe.py: at n = 2 … 8 there are 1351 compositions with both contexts non-empty and the overlap-length histogram is len1 only — zero exceptions. (The same probe reproduces §4k's shape counts from an independent implementation: 16 rules → 13 distinct leading monomials → 58 shapes = 45 proper + 13 degenerate at n = 4.)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The reason is a single invariant. Every rule's leading monomial begins with its largest letter — [σᵢ, σᵢ], [σⱼ, σᵢ, σⱼ] at j = i + 1, [σᵢ, σⱼ] at j + 1 < i, and descWord i j ++ [σᵢ], which descWord_cons opens as σᵢ :: (descWord i' j ++ [σᵢ]). That is lm_head_is_max. Apply it to rule₂ and the overlap's head dominates every letter of the overlap; but the overlap is a suffix of lm₁, so for a Bokut–Shiao rule₁ its head lies strictly inside the descending run once the overlap is longer than one letter, where every index is at most i − 1. The trailing σᵢ is in the overlap either way, and the two bounds collide.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                overlap_length_one_of_bs_left is that argument for a Bokut–Shiao rule₁ — the one shape whose leading monomial has unbounded length, and the one CornerGeneral composes. The other three rule₁ shapes have leading monomials of length 2 or 3 and are not proved here.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                ↑y.index ≤ ↑h.index
