                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.aside_to_sweptWord {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i'' i' i : Fin n} (h₂ : ↑i'' + 1 = ↑i') (h₁ : ↑i' + 1 = ↑i) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(descWord i ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ bsWord₂ i' i ⟨0, hn⟩, c)]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [([{ index := i'' }, { index := i' }, { index := i }] ++ pairSweep i' ⟨0, hn⟩, c)])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Side A of the deep self-overlap, swept. The three-step head lands on a doubled descending run, and §4bo's sweep takes it from there — so side A costs 3 + (i − 1) steps to here, not the (i²+i+4)/2 the greedy reduction spends reaching its own split word.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    §4bq The far-commutation carry — side A's tail, inner loop #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    What remains of side A after §4bp is a tail of pure far commutation, and its shape was measured rather than guessed. Grouped by top index, the rules are

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    (2,0), then (3,1) (3,0), then (4,2) (4,1) (4,0), … , then (i, i−2) … (i, 0)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    — at consecutive positions, m − 1 steps for each m from 2 to i, which is the measured i(i−1)/2. Each group is one generator carried rightward past a descending run, so the inner loop is a single lemma and the outer loop is a second induction over m.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    gen_past_descWord is that inner loop: σ_m · descWord k z ⟶* descWord k z · σ_m whenever k + 1 < m, one step per letter, induction on the gap k − z.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Two things about the tail are measured and worth keeping:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • The two branches of the split run the same chain — not merely the same shape. Compared as full rule-and-position sequences (not as labels, which hide a rule's lower index and have misled this bean twice), they are identical at i = 3, 4, 5, 6. The branches differ only by a trailing σ₀, which no rule in the tail touches. So the tail is one lemma with the trailing context as a parameter, which the step lemmas already carry as b.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    • Side B's tail is NOT side A's. Its per-branch length is (i²−i+4)/2, exactly two more than A's i(i−1)/2 at every i tested, which reads like B's branches reducing onto A's in two steps. They do not: checked to i = 6, no B-branch reaches its A-counterpart at all. Two separate tails.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.gen_past_descWord' {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) (m : Fin n) (d : ℕ) (k z : Fin n) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ↑k = ↑z + d → ↑k + 1 < ↑m → ∀ (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (a b : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c : ℝ), c ≠ 0 → CtxAvoids (L₁ ++ L₂) a b → MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (a ++ [{ index := m }] ++ descWord k z ++ b, c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (a ++ descWord k z ++ [{ index := m }] ++ b, c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    gen_past_descWord, carrying arbitrary surrounding terms.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.gen_past_descWord {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) (m : Fin n) (d : ℕ) (k z : Fin n) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    ↑k = ↑z + d → ↑k + 1 < ↑m → ∀ (a b : Monomial (HeckeGen n)) (c : ℝ), c ≠ 0 → MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(a ++ [{ index := m }] ++ descWord k z ++ b, c)]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(a ++ descWord k z ++ [{ index := m }] ++ b, c)])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    A far generator commutes rightward past a whole descending run.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    σ_m · descWord k z ⟶* descWord k z · σ_m whenever k + 1 < m, by one far-commutation step per letter of the run. The induction is on the gap k − z, as descWord_split_aux's is.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    §4br The unshuffle — and side A of hdeep, complete #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    §4bq gave the carry; this is the loop that uses it, and with it side A closes end to end.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    The unshuffle. pairList m z — the interleaved pairs σ_{m−1}σ_m σ_{m−2}σ_{m−1} ⋯ σ_zσ_{z+1}, i.e. pairSweep without its trailing σ_zσ_z — separates into two descending runs:

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    pairList m z ⟶* descWord (m−1) z ++ (descWord m z).dropLast

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    one gen_past_descWord per level. The induction hypothesis separates the pairs below, and then the top pair's upper letter σ_m is carried rightward across the lower run it now sits in front of. The base case is m = z + 1, where a single pair σ_zσ_m is already descWord z z ++ (descWord m z).dropLast and no step is needed.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Writing the upper run as (descWord m z).dropLast — the run with its bottom letter removed — is what keeps z + 1 from ever having to be named as a Fin n.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Side A, complete. §4bp's head, then the unshuffle, then one last carry: σ_i leaves the leading block and crosses the lower run, which turns σ_{i−2}σ_{i−1} ++ descWord (i−2) 0 into bsWord₂ (i−2) (i−1) 0 and σ_i ++ (descWord (i−1) 0).dropLast into (descWord i 0).dropLast. What is left is one word ending in σ₀σ₀, and the single quadratic step of the whole reduction fires there, giving

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    NF + (q − q⁻¹)·(NF · σ₀), NF = bsWord₂ (i−2) (i−1) 0 · (descWord i 0).dropLast

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    which is the two-term normal form the probe measured. Every step before that one is monomial, exactly as the rule census said.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    So aside_resolves discharges side A of hdeep in full, general in i. Side B is done to its split word (§4bo) and still needs its tail — the same carry sequence shifted by one, plus two Bokut–Shiao steps — and then the two-term bookkeeping joins the halves.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    def UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.pairList {n : ℕ} (m z : Fin n) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Monomial (HeckeGen n)

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    σ_{m−1}σ_m σ_{m−2}σ_{m−1} ⋯ σ_zσ_{z+1} — pairSweep without its trailing σ_zσ_z, i.e. the interleaved pairs alone. Zipped against the run's own tail, so again no arithmetic on Fin n.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The interleaved pairs unshuffle into two descending runs.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      pairList m z ⟶* descWord (m−1) z ++ (descWord m z).dropLast, by one gen_past_descWord carry per level: the induction hypothesis separates the pairs below, and then σ_m — the upper letter of the top pair — is carried rightward past the whole lower run it now sits in front of.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      (descWord m z).dropLast is the run with its bottom letter removed, which is the upper run; writing it that way avoids naming z + 1.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      pairSweep is pairList with the trailing σ_zσ_z — the pairs, then the one place the quadratic rule can fire.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(descWord i ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ bsWord₂ i' i ⟨0, hn⟩, c)]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(bsWord₂ i'' i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ List.dropLast (descWord i ⟨0, hn⟩) ++ [{ index := ⟨0, hn⟩ }], c * (hp.q - hp.q⁻¹)), (bsWord₂ i'' i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ List.dropLast (descWord i ⟨0, hn⟩), c)])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Side A of the deep self-overlap resolves, in full. One word, then the single quadratic step, landing on the two-term element NF + (q − q⁻¹)·(NF · σ₀) with NF = bsWord₂ (i−2) (i−1) 0 · (descWord i 0).dropLast. Everything before that step is monomial.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      §4bs Side B, complete — and both halves of hdeep land on one element #

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      §4br closed side A. This closes side B, on exactly the element side A reaches.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      bside_to_split runs §4bo's route to the split word, rewrites it through pairSweep_eq into pairs-plus-σ₀σ₀, unshuffles the pairs with §4br's pairList_unshuffle, and fires the one quadratic step. So both sides use the same unshuffle; only the context it runs in differs, which is what the earlier measurement meant by "the same carry sequence shifted by one".

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      bside_branch is the tail, and it is one lemma parameterised by j: the trailing σ_i closes descWord i j into bsWord₁ i j, and after that rule fires, the σ_{i'} its bsWord₂ puts down closes descWord i' 0 into bsWord₁ i' 0 for a second. j = 0 on the H-branch and j = 1 on the 1-branch — that single index is the whole difference between them, and it is the extra σ₀ the split leaves behind. Predicted from the measurement in §4bq and confirmed here.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The two-term bookkeeping, handled by length. After the split there are two terms, so monicStep's side condition is no longer vacuous. Rather than compare words, bside_branch takes a single hypothesis — every surrounding term has a length other than this word's — and discharges both of its steps from it, since Bokut–Shiao is monic and all three words of the chain have the same length. The two branch words differ in length by exactly one (that same σ₀), so each serves as the other's witness. descWord_length is what makes this arithmetic; it is proved on the gap like everything else about descWord.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Both targets are the same element, via [σ_i] ++ descWord i' 0 = descWord i 0 and (descWord i 0).dropLast ++ [σ₀] = descWord i 0. What is left of hdeep is the joining: running the two chains inside the S-polynomial's two terms, where each side's chain carries the other side's term as context.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.descWord_length {n : ℕ} (d : ℕ) {i j : Fin n} :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      ↑i = ↑j + d → List.length (descWord i j) = ↑i - ↑j + 1

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The length of a descending run. |descWord i j| = i − j + 1. Proved on the gap, like everything else about descWord.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      source
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.bside_to_split' {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i' i : Fin n} (h₁ : ↑i' + 1 = ↑i) (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (hCh : CtxAvoids (L₁ ++ L₂) [{ index := i' }] []) (hCt : CtxAvoids (L₁ ++ L₂) [] [{ index := ⟨0, hn⟩ }, { index := ⟨0, hn⟩ }, { index := i }]) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (bsWord₂ i' i ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ [{ index := i }], c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ List.dropLast (descWord i ⟨0, hn⟩) ++ [{ index := ⟨0, hn⟩ }] ++ [{ index := i }], c * (hp.q - hp.q⁻¹)) :: (descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ List.dropLast (descWord i ⟨0, hn⟩) ++ [{ index := i }], c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      bside_to_split, carrying arbitrary surrounding terms.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Two hypotheses, of two different shapes, and the second is not optional. The sweep and the quadratic step both act with a fixed prefix in front, so a head condition covers them. The unshuffle acts at the left end of the word — a = [] — so nothing sits in front of it to separate on, and what protects it is the word's right end instead: no surrounding word may end in σ₀σ₀σ_i.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(bsWord₂ i' i ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ [{ index := i }], c)]) (AlgElement.ofTerms [(descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ List.dropLast (descWord i ⟨0, hn⟩) ++ [{ index := ⟨0, hn⟩ }] ++ [{ index := i }], c * (hp.q - hp.q⁻¹)), (descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ List.dropLast (descWord i ⟨0, hn⟩) ++ [{ index := i }], c)])

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      List.length (descWord i j) = ↑i - ↑j + 1

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.bside_branch_core {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i'' i' i j : Fin n} (h₂ : ↑i'' + 1 = ↑i') (h₁ : ↑i' + 1 = ↑i) (hj : ↑j ≤ ↑i') (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (hne0 : ∀ q ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), q ≠ descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ descWord i j ++ [{ index := i }]) (hne1 : ∀ q ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), q ≠ descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ bsWord₂ i' i j) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ descWord i j ++ [{ index := i }], c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (bsWord₂ i'' i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ [{ index := i }] ++ descWord i' j, c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      One branch of side B's tail, with its two side conditions raw.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      bside_branch derives both from a length hypothesis. That is the right discharge inside side B, where every word of the chain has the same length, but it is the wrong one at the joining: side A's normal form has exactly the lengths side B's post-split words do. Both words entering a step here open with descWord i' 0, so a head condition discharges them too — and a caller that needs one shape for the ambient terms and the other for side B's own supplies whichever it has.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.bside_branch {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i'' i' i j : Fin n} (h₂ : ↑i'' + 1 = ↑i') (h₁ : ↑i' + 1 = ↑i) (hj : ↑j ≤ ↑i') (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (hlen : ∀ w ∈ List.map Prod.fst (L₁ ++ L₂), List.length w ≠ ↑i' + 1 + (↑i - ↑j + 1) + 1) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ descWord i j ++ [{ index := i }], c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (bsWord₂ i'' i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ [{ index := i }] ++ descWord i' j, c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      One branch of side B's tail: two Bokut–Shiao steps.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      descWord i' 0 · descWord i j · σ_i ⟶* bsWord₂ i'' i' 0 · σ_i · descWord i' j, for either j — j = 0 on the H-branch and j = 1 on the 1-branch, which is the only way the two differ. The trailing σ_i closes descWord i j into bsWord₁ i j; after that rule fires, descWord i' 0 is closed by the σ_{i'} its bsWord₂ put down, and the second rule fires on that.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The surrounding terms are arbitrary, subject only to a length condition: every one of them must have a length other than this word's. All three words in the chain have the same length — Bokut–Shiao is monic and length-preserving — so that single hypothesis discharges both steps' side conditions.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      theorem UGB.GrobnerShirshov.Hecke.bside_resolves' {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (hp : HeckeParams) {i'' i' i : Fin n} (h₂ : ↑i'' + 1 = ↑i') (h₁ : ↑i' + 1 = ↑i) (L₁ L₂ : List (Monomial (HeckeGen n) × ℝ)) (c : ℝ) (hc : c ≠ 0) (hCh : CtxAvoids (L₁ ++ L₂) [{ index := i' }] []) (hCt : CtxAvoids (L₁ ++ L₂) [] [{ index := ⟨0, hn⟩ }, { index := ⟨0, hn⟩ }, { index := i }]) :
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      MultiStepReduction (heckeOrder n) (heckeCompletedRewritingSystem n hn hp) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (bsWord₂ i' i ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ [{ index := i }], c) :: L₂)) (AlgElement.ofTerms (L₁ ++ (bsWord₂ i'' i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ [{ index := i }] ++ descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩, c * (hp.q - hp.q⁻¹)) :: (bsWord₂ i'' i' ⟨0, hn⟩ ++ [{ index := i }] ++ List.dropLast (descWord i' ⟨0, hn⟩), c) :: L₂))

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      bside_resolves, carrying arbitrary surrounding terms.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      The two hypotheses are exactly bside_to_split''s. The branch steps need nothing further from the caller: their side conditions against the ambient terms follow from the head condition, and their side conditions against side B's own other term follow from a length count internal to this proof.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      source
